results.alertTitle: AWS console sign-in by backdoor-svc from an external address

summary.tpReason: CloudTrail directly corroborates two successful ConsoleLogin events for backdoor-svc, both without MFA, and shows the account was created and granted AdministratorAccess minutes earlier by mirage from 198.51.100.42. The surrounding actions are unequivocally hostile: data access, resource abuse, security-group exposure, persistence, and CloudTrail tampering.
summary.fpReason: No credible benign explanation is supported. The account name, creation sequence, active access key, AdministratorAccess attachment, MFA absence, two external successful logins, and log deletion are inconsistent with routine administration.
summary.whatHappened: On 2026-08-19, IAM user mirage logged in successfully from 198.51.100.42 at 16:49:17Z without MFA in AWS account 123456789012. Mirage created IAM user backdoor-svc at 16:53:35Z, created active access key AKIAI99ATTACKKEY at 16:54:07Z, attached arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AdministratorAccess at 16:55:20Z, opened security group sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 to 0.0.0.0/0, launched five p3.16xlarge instances, read finance/2026-budget-final.xlsx, hr/employee-records-full.csv, and secrets/api-keys-production.json from corp-data-prod, stopped and deleted management-events-trail, and created a login profile with no password reset at 17:16:50Z. Backdoor-svc then logged in successfully without MFA at 17:19:20Z from 198.51.100.42 and at 17:24:05Z from 203.0.113.77, followed by DescribeInstances at 17:26:25Z. User-data was changed to fetch and execute an external shell script.
keyEvidence: AWSCloudTrail: successful, MFA=false ConsoleLogin for backdoor-svc at 2026-08-19 17:19:20Z from 198.51.100.42 and 17:24:05Z from 203.0.113.77; both have empty ErrorCode and ResponseElements ConsoleLogin=Success.
AWSCloudTrail: mirage created backdoor-svc, an active access key, AdministratorAccess, and a login profile between 16:53:35Z and 17:16:50Z; all activity originated at 198.51.100.42 with MFA=false.
AWSCloudTrail: mirage successfully launched five p3.16xlarge instances, opened sg-0a1b2c3d4e5f67890 to 0.0.0.0/0, and read three sensitive S3 objects at 17:00:35Z-17:04:07Z.
AWSCloudTrail: mirage stopped logging at 17:05:25Z and deleted management-events-trail at 17:10:35Z; this is evidence of deliberate defense evasion and creates a likely audit gap.
AWSCloudTrail: backdoor-svc used 203.0.113.77 with aws-cli to DescribeInstances at 17:26:25Z after the second successful login; no errors were recorded.
The alert record b11a4e1c-59b3-75e1-3c95-c068a1548765 matches the two successful logins and source addresses exactly. No MFA evidence was present in the corroborating CloudTrail records.
researchDone: Queried AWSCloudTrail for the alert window and confirmed both successful ConsoleLogin events, identities, source IPs, user agents, MFA state, and errors.
Queried AWSCloudTrail for the preceding 40 minutes from both source IPs and reconstructed the mirage-to-backdoor-svc account creation and privilege-escalation sequence.
Reviewed IAM, EC2, S3, and CloudTrail management events for 2026-08-19; found sensitive object reads, five instance launches, public ingress, user-data modification, and trail deletion.
Queried post-alert AWSCloudTrail through 18:30Z for backdoor-svc; found DescribeInstances from 203.0.113.77 and no recorded errors.
Checked same-day account-creation, access-key, policy-attachment, login-profile, console-login, and trail-tampering events; no benign owner or MFA corroboration was present.
Checked SecurityAlert for the alert ID and related backdoor-svc alerts in the surrounding period; this alert is present and its stored details match CloudTrail.
